name: Restaurant Franchise and Expansion Pitch Deck
description: A bold restaurant-franchise pitch connecting brand and consumer demand to store formats, menu system, site strategy, unit economics, expansion sequencing, franchise support, team credentials, and partnership terms.
style_guide:
# Restaurant Franchise and Expansion Pitch Deck

## Design intent

Create a confident franchise pitch that proves repeatability rather than merely celebrating food and growth. The narrative should connect brand relevance and consumer demand to a controlled menu, store formats, site criteria, supply capacity, unit economics, expansion gates, operator support, governance, and commercial terms. Cream analytical pages keep the system inspectable; charcoal fields carry maps and decisive partnership messages; flame orange identifies growth and hero actions; mustard gold distinguishes secondary stages and operating support.

The previews establish visual direction only. Do not reuse their restaurant, founder, cities, store count, menu, products, prices, sales, margins, payback, fees, royalties, expansion dates, team, territories, or partner terms. Rebuild every fact and claim from the current workspace.

## Canvas, grid, and spacing

- Use a fixed `1280 × 720 px` 16:9 canvas with `48–60 px` side margins, `28–36 px` top framing, and compact source notes.
- Use a 12-column grid with `16–20 px` gutters. Align brand evidence, format cards, product captions, maps, site criteria, KPI cards, P&L bars, uses of funds, support stages, team rows, and term summaries.
- Reserve `95–130 px` for a numbered eyebrow, conclusion-first title, and one commercial framing line.
- Favor one dominant system per page: brand evidence with a trend panel, three store formats with a product rail, map with phased market logic, or KPI strip over economics and capital allocation.
- Use square cards, hard rules, no shadow, and bold contrast. Food photography should support product proof without turning the deck into a menu.

## Color system

- Menu cream: `#F4EEE4` for analytical canvases and warm hospitality.
- Grill black: `#1C130F` for the cover, market maps, support pages, headers, and primary type.
- Flame orange: `#E44B27` for growth targets, hero products, selected markets, conversion gates, and decisive actions.
- Mustard gold: `#D79A2B` for support stages, secondary formats, and operational milestones.
- Olive: `#68743D` only for verified readiness, mature operations, or completed stages.
- Orange signals the primary commercial path; gold supports sequencing. Green must never imply readiness without evidence.

## Typography

- Use `Inter`, `Arial`, `Helvetica Neue`, or another bold modern sans-serif.
- Cover title: `50–66 px`; page headline: `32–42 px`; body: `12–16 px`; product and financial tables: `10–13 px`; sources and qualifiers: `8–10 px`; KPI values: `28–38 px`.
- Use strong bold weights for the commercial thesis and selective italics for one action phrase or strategic contrast.
- Use uppercase tracking for section labels, format codes, stages, terms, and evidence metadata.
- Apply tabular numerals to store counts, area, seats, capex, staffing, price, sales, margin, payback, fees, royalty, dates, and territories.

## Components and exhibits

- Brand pages should connect founding evidence, signature product or method, operational discipline, consumer trend, and current footprint.
- Store-format cards need footprint, seats or throughput, capex, staffing, service model, menu scope, dayparts, unit economics, and site context.
- Product cards should identify verified item, role, recipe control, ingredient dependencies, preparation time, price basis, margin definition, and status.
- Expansion maps must distinguish operating stores, signed sites, target markets, supply reach, territory boundaries, and timing.
- Site filters should include demand, catchment, visibility, access, occupancy cost, delivery, competition, utilities, licenses, labor, and supply feasibility.
- Unit-economics pages must reconcile sales, COGS, labor, occupancy, marketing, other operating expense, store EBITDA, capex, working capital, and payback.
- Support plans should show territory and site, design, training, opening, supply and operations, marketing, technology, audit, and ongoing growth ownership.
- Partnership panels must separate initial fee, investment, royalty, marketing contribution, territory, term, renewal, obligations, and next diligence step.

## Page families

### Food-led franchise cover

Use one rights-cleared hero-product image on a dark field with the restaurant, round or purpose, presenter, company, date, confidentiality, current footprint, and the central expansion question.

### Brand story and consumer trend

Pair an authentic restaurant or operations image with concise brand proof and a dark trend panel. Separate company evidence from external consumer research.

### Store formats and hero products

Use three comparable format cards and a narrow product rail. Show what remains standardized across formats and what changes by demand, footprint, and service occasion.

### Target markets and site strategy

Combine a dark geographic footprint with a phased expansion plan and mandatory site filters. Explain why supply capacity, people, and brand density support the sequence.

### Unit economics and expansion plan

Lead with four comparable KPIs, then reconcile the store P&L, capital use, and gated store-count plan. Show mature and new-store cohorts separately.

### Franchise support and partnership

Use a dark operating page with a staged support journey, accountable team, clear division of franchisor and franchisee responsibilities, commercial terms, and a specific next diligence action.

## Imagery and mapping

- Use rights-cleared photography of actual food, restaurants, kitchens, teams, packaging, and service moments.
- Preserve accurate product size, ingredients, preparation, and color. Label prototypes, seasonal items, and illustrative formats.
- Maps need geography, scale, market status, supply assumptions, and source date.
- Avoid unrelated food photography, empty luxury interiors, stock founders, or fabricated store and customer scenes.

## Content integrity and franchise discipline

- Do not invent restaurants, openings, closures, reviews, stores, sales, margins, prices, recipes, suppliers, capex, staffing, payback, fees, royalties, territories, partners, or growth commitments.
- Distinguish company-owned, franchised, licensed, signed, under construction, planned, target, and illustrative locations.
- Define sales period, comparable-store cohort, gross or net revenue, tax basis, discounts, delivery commissions, and currency.
- Unit economics must disclose store maturity, format, geography, sample size, median or average, owner compensation, depreciation, financing, tax, and central allocations.
- Payback requires initial investment, working capital, ramp, maintenance capex, cash-flow definition, and timing method. Do not present best-store results as typical.
- Verify food safety, allergens, nutrition, labeling, labor, licensing, lease, fire, accessibility, data, delivery-platform, advertising, franchise-disclosure, competition, and territory obligations.
- Expansion targets require site pipeline, supply capacity, training capacity, leadership, technology, capital, approvals, and stop/go gates.
- The governing disclosure and signed agreements control. A deck must not imply guaranteed sales, profitability, payback, territory, financing, or approval.

## Avoid

- Do not copy preview brand names, products, stores, markets, economics, costs, support stages, team, fees, royalties, territories, or dates.
- Do not sell expansion on food photography and store count without cohort economics, supply readiness, operator capability, and risk.
- Do not compare formats using inconsistent maturity, geography, cost allocation, or revenue definitions.
- Do not hide delivery commissions, labor, occupancy, pre-opening, maintenance, owner time, or central charges.
- Do not use glossy gradients, glass cards, heavy shadows, 3D charts, decorative maps, star ratings without sources, or unreadable legal notes.
